coreStoryFacts.text: Coinbase and Circle Internet dropped between 3 and 4% as the 10-year Treasury yield hit 4.79%, hammering high-beta crypto stocks while Bitcoin sat flat.
No fresh company-specific news explains the declines in any of the three names this morning.

Monday's rally was led by a Bitmine treasury disclosure showing holdings of 5,901,112 Ethereum tokens, or 4.9% of total supply, putting it 98% of the way to its stated goal of owning 5% of all Ethereum.
The morning economic data window and afternoon commentary from Fed officials will shape whether long yields hold near current levels.
A yield reversal lower could bring quick relief to Circle Internet, Bitmine, and Coinbase given how tightly they have moved with rates this morning.
Extended pressure at the long end would keep the beta trade under strain regardless of what Bitcoin and Ethereum prices do next.
Circle Internet Group ( NYSE:CRCL ) stock is down 4% to $91.80, reversing part of Monday's 10% rally.
Meanwhile, Bitmine Immersion Technologies ( NYSE:BMNR ) shares are falling 4% to $24.38 after climbing 6% in the prior session.
Coinbase Global ( NASDAQ:COIN ) stock is sliding 3% to $182.20, unwinding a 5% Monday advance.
The catalyst is in the bond market rather than the crypto tape.

Bitmine in particular offers no operating buffer if Ethereum turns lower, so smaller allocations and defined stop levels make sense for anyone taking exposure into a volatile rate backdrop (we wrote a free playbook on keeping speculative positions capped at 5% with real exit rules, here).
The CBOE Volatility Index or VIX sits at 15.96, a mediuim-volatility reading that argues against a market-wide fear event.
Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) and Ethereum (CRYPTO:ETH) sit essentially flat this Tuesday morning, yet the equities tied to them are opening sharply lower.
It's the second consecutive session in which crypto stocks have traded independently of the coins they typically shadow, and this time the move runs to the downside rather than higher.
It also explains why the equity moves are running several multiples ahead of IBIT and QQQ, both of which face the same rate pressure without the beta profile.
The trio does very different things, so a rates shock should not hit them identically.
Circle Internet earns reserve income on the short-dated Treasury assets backing USDC, so higher yields are actually a tailwind for the underlying business even as its stock trades lower.
Coinbase generates transaction and subscription revenue tied to platform activity, so its results track trading volumes rather than any single coin price.
The iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF ( NASDAQ:IBIT ) is down 1.41% to $44.04.
The Invesco QQQ Trust ( NASDAQ:QQQ ) is off 1.32% to $707.27, so the three crypto equities are falling harder than either the Bitcoin fund or large-cap tech.
Circle Internet deserves special attention in that context.

The company's reserve model means each additional basis point on short-term Treasuries flows toward its bottom line, so today's selloff in Circle Internet stock runs in the opposite direction of the fundamental setup for Circle Internet's business.
That gap is the kind of dislocation traders remember once yields settle.
Its stock tracks the market value of an Ethereum treasury rather than an operating business, so when coins sit flat, there's nothing to offset a risk-off tape.

sources.title: Strategy and Riot Fall 4%, Cipher Digital Declines 3% as MSCI Index Rules and Convertible Sale Weigh - AOL.com
passages: An index decision and a fresh debt sale are pulling two crypto-linked names lower.
Strategy ( NASDAQ:MSTR ) stock is down 4% to $145.50 during the morning session after an index rule change from MSCI ( NYSE:MSCI ).
Strategy (MSTR) faces MSCI index exclusion risk at the November review, while Cipher Digital (CIFR) drops 3% after pricing zero-coupon convertible notes for Barber Lake.

As a Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) miner, Riot runs a different model from both, since Strategy holds the token as its main treasury asset and Cipher Digital is converting former Bitcoin mining sites into AI data centers.
MSCI announced revised index eligibility rules for non-operating companies, replacing interim limits on companies with large digital asset reserves with financial tests.
Those tests take effect with MSCI's November index review, and Strategy is among the companies MSCI previously identified as potentially ineligible.
ETFs tied to MSCI equity indexes held a record $2.818 trillion at the end of Q2 2026.
As the largest corporate holder of Bitcoin, Strategy reported 846,000 bitcoin on its books as of Q2, plus $6.7 billion in convertible debt.
Strategy shares are falling even with Bitcoin at $81,903 and higher over the past 24 hours, a split that puts the index question at the center of the selloff.
That pressure leaves Strategy stock down 5% year to date (YTD).
For Cipher Digital, the open variable is execution on the data center projects its new notes fund.
Investors should consider keeping their position sizes modest until MSCI's decision on Strategy settles.
A stronger Bitcoin price may not offset index-driven selling in Strategy shares if MSCI moves to exclude the company.
CleanSpark (CLSK) signed a $6.6 billion, 20-year lease as WGMI slides 2%, weighed down by Cipher Digital's dominant 18% fund position.
The upside for Strategy rests on MSCI's rule that current index members are removed only after failing its screen in two consecutive annual filing periods.

A slide in Ethereum ( CRYPTO:ETH ) is pulling crypto-linked stocks lower, and two very different business models are taking almost identical hits. In morning trading, Cipher Digital ( NASDAQ:CIFR ) stock is at $6.27, down 4%. The company mines Bitcoin ( CRYPTO:BTC ) and is shifting to leasing high-performance computing (HPC) data centers to large cloud operators and artificial intelligence firms, yet the stock is moving in step with digital-asset prices. Two other crypto names are sliding alongside Cipher Digital. That pairing shows how tightly the market is linking crypto miners, coin holders and AI-infrastructure builders during a risk-off stretch. Ethereum is at $2,117.85, down 5.4% over the past 24 hours. Bitcoin is at $74,641, down 1.7% over the same stretch, so Ethereum’s drop is markedly steeper. Crypto is whipsawing on a scandal tied to NVIDIA ( NASDAQ:NVDA | NVDA Price Prediction ) and on Iran tensions, with the sell-off sparking a liquidation wave. Risk-off sentiment spilling over from tech is weighing on assets that trade on momentum, and crypto sits near the front of that line. The pressure adds to a drawdown that dates to October 10, which Bitmine Immersion Technologies ( NYSE:BMNR ) described as the largest single-day liquidation event in crypto’s history. Thomas Lee is Bitmine’s chairman. He has said that “crypto prices stage V-shaped recoveries after a lingering and drawn out decline, and we expect this to again be the case in this current drawdown.” Bitmine stock is at $17.97, down 4%. As an Ethereum treasury company, Bitmine gives shareholders direct exposure to the coin, which makes it the purest proxy for Ethereum’s slide among the three featured names. The company disclosed on November 9 that its Ethereum holdings reached 6.07 million tokens, with total crypto plus cash and marketable securities of $14.3 billion. Strategy ( NASDAQ:MSTR ) stock is at $124.90, down 3%. With 848,517 BTC on its balance sheet, the company tracks Bitcoin, whose milder decline lines up with a smaller drop in the stock. Cipher Digital cuts against that pattern, posting a decline in line with Bitmine’s despite its Bitcoin focus. Another miner converting bitcoin-mining sites for AI cloud capacity is at $20.80, down 4%, falling faster than Strategy Inc. as well. A major crypto exchange’s stock is at $131.94, down 2%. A smaller Ethereum treasury company is at $5.95, down 5%, according to CryptoProwl. That’s the steepest decline in the group, and it fits the broader pattern of Ethereum-heavy names falling harder than Bitcoin-focused ones. Cipher Digital is turning itself into a landlord for AI compute. The company still mines bitcoin, but its growth plan centers on long-term leases with hyperscaler tenants at sites such as Black Pearl, Barber Lake and Stingray. That pivot puts it among certain key suppliers. The power, cooling and networking suppliers are quietly feeding the data-center expansion (we covered seven of them in a free report on AI infrastructure names that aren’t chipmakers ). Compared with its two crypto peers, Cipher Digital keeps a lighter coin treasury, so the stock’s link to crypto prices runs through its mining legacy and investor perception. Bitmine occupies the other end of the spectrum, with a balance sheet built around Ethereum and a Made-in-America Validator Network (MAVAN) staking expansion designed to put those tokens to work. Strategy Inc. blends its bitcoin treasury with a legacy enterprise analytics software business and a growing Digital Credit preferred-stock platform. That mix gives Strategy Inc. more than one lever, though Bitcoin’s price still drives its earnings. The next test for Cipher Digital is whether its data halls deliver on schedule between Q4 2026 and Q1 2027, which could loosen the stock’s tie to crypto sentiment. For Bitmine, investors need to see Ethereum stabilize after a decline steeper than Bitcoin’s. Bulls can point to Cipher Digital’s amended 20-year Barber Lake lease, which lifted the site’s contracted revenue to about $9.1 billion, and to Lee’s call for a V-shaped recovery at Bitmine. The bears note that Cipher Digital carries about $6.7 billion of total debt , and Bitmine’s treasury value moves directly with Ethereum’s price. A turn in crypto sentiment could move Bitmine and Cipher Digital just as quickly in the other direction. The World Wide Technology Championship prize-money payout breakdown shows a payout of 18 percent of the purse to the winner, and how much each PGA Tour player earns is guaranteed down to the last-place professional player. The 2026 World Wide Technology Championship field is headed by Ben James, Ryan Gerard, Chris Kirk and more. This tournament started with 120 players, and a cut was made this week after two rounds to the top 65 players and ties. Every professional player in the field is paid for completing the event, but how much each player is paid at the 2026 World Wide Technology Championship from the correct 2026 World Wide Technology Championship full-field payout is based on their finish in this event. The 2026 World Wide Technology Championship prize money payout is set ahead of the event. In events with a cut, the PGA Tour will add money to the purse, with the PGA Tour paying out money from the purse if more than, in this case, 65 professionals make the cut to ensure all players are paid. What else is on the line Beyond money, there are important points, perks and benefits on the line for the field -- in particular, the tournament winner. extraction.body: Los Cabos, Mexico – 19 year old Blades Brown has won the World Wide Technology Championship at El Cardonal at Diamante golf course. Brown won with a score of 23 under par in a playoff over Ben James. This is his Brown’s first career win. Ben James eagled his 18th hole on Sunday to force a playoff with Brown, who was in the clubhouse with the lead. The pair birdied the par 5 18th, which was the first playoff hole. They went back to 18 for the second playoff hole. Brown and James both had chips from similar positions. James ended up outside Brown and missed his putt. Brown made the four footer for his first win. This was Brown’s 22nd career start on the PGA Tour. He is the youngest winner on Tour since 1931. This win gives him PGA Tour Exemption through 2028. Brown shot a final round 63 to win the tournament by one shot. This is the fourth year in a row where the winner of the World Wide Technology Championship has shot a 63 in the final round. Ben Griffin won it last year, and Austin Eckroat and Erik Van Rooyen in 2024 and 2023. Brown won with a combination of strong driving and lights out putting. In driving, he gained 4 strokes on the field, and he had 8 strokes gained: putting. He hit 94% of his fairways, which strangely was only good enough for 18th place. Michael Kim was one shot away from the magic number of a final round 63. He shot a final round 64 to finish second at 22 under. His strokes gained: driving was -.67, and that was the main difference between him and Brown. Next up on tour is the Austin Championship presented by Compliance Solutions. This is the first year of this tournament. It takes place at the Fazio Canyons Course at Omni Barton Creek Resort & Spa. Driver: Callaway Quantum Triple Diamond (9°) ( Mitsubishi Kai’li White 70 TX ) We believe that golf is better when golfers are better informed. passages: Los Cabos, Mexico – 19 year old Blades Brown has won the World Wide Technology Championship at El Cardonal at Diamante golf course. Brown won with a score of 23 under par in a playoff over Ben James. This is his Brown’s first career win.

Ben James eagled his 18th hole on Sunday to force a playoff with Brown, who was in the clubhouse with the lead. The pair birdied the par 5 18th, which was the first playoff hole. They went back to 18 for the second playoff hole. Brown and James both had chips from similar positions. James ended up outside Brown and missed his putt. Brown made the four footer for his first win.
This was Brown’s 22nd career start on the PGA Tour. He is the youngest winner on Tour since 1931. This win gives him PGA Tour Exemption through 2028.

Brown shot a final round 63 to win the tournament by one shot. This is the fourth year in a row where the winner of the World Wide Technology Championship has shot a 63 in the final round. Ben Griffin won it last year, and Austin Eckroat and Erik Van Rooyen in 2024 and 2023.

Brown won with a combination of strong driving and lights out putting. In driving, he gained 4 strokes on the field, and he had 8 strokes gained: putting. He hit 94% of his fairways, which strangely was only good enough for 18th place.

Michael Kim was one shot away from the magic number of a final round 63. He shot a final round 64 to finish second at 22 under. His strokes gained: driving was -.67, and that was the main difference between him and Brown.
Next up on tour is the Austin Championship presented by Compliance Solutions. This is the first year of this tournament. It takes place at the Fazio Canyons Course at Omni Barton Creek Resort & Spa.

extraction.body: Los Cabos, Mexico – 19 year old Blades Brown has won the World Wide Technology Championship at El Cardonal at Diamante golf course. Brown won with a score of 23 under par in a playoff over Ben James. This is his Brown’s first career win. Ben James eagled his 18th hole on Sunday to force a playoff with Brown, who was in the clubhouse with the lead. The pair birdied the par 5 18th, which was the first playoff hole. They went back to 18 for the second playoff hole. Brown and James both had chips from similar positions. James ended up outside Brown and missed his putt. Brown made the four footer for his first win. This was Brown’s 22nd career start on the PGA Tour. He is the youngest winner on Tour since 1931. This win gives him PGA Tour Exemption through 2028. Brown shot a final round 63 to win the tournament by one shot. This is the fourth year in a row where the winner of the World Wide Technology Championship has shot a 63 in the final round. Ben Griffin won it last year, and Austin Eckroat and Erik Van Rooyen in 2024 and 2023. Brown won with a combination of strong driving and lights out putting. In driving, he gained 4 strokes on the field, and he had 8 strokes gained: putting. He hit 94% of his fairways, which strangely was only good enough for 18th place. Michael Kim was one shot away from the magic number of a final round 63. He shot a final round 64 to finish second at 22 under. His strokes gained: driving was -.67, and that was the main difference between him and Brown. Next up on tour is the Austin Championship presented by Compliance Solutions. This is the first year of this tournament. It takes place at the Fazio Canyons Course at Omni Barton Creek Resort & Spa. These rising exchange deposits signal a boost in selling pressure from long-term holders - a trend that traders are keeping an eye on as BTC strives to seek a stable footing..Ethereum ETF Demand Falls Sharply.According to investment firm Matrixport, inflows into Ethereum ETFs have cooled down dramatically. Monthly inflows fell from over $5 billion during the summer to $600 million in October.Recent buying has become highly concentrated, with Bitmine now responsible for most of the new ETF inflows. Bitcoin's inability to reclaim key technical support levels adds to increased selling from long-term holders, suggesting the near-term pressure may persist. The jobs report set the course for markets as investors try to find their footing and face deeper corrections in crypto prices..FAQs.1. Comments from Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent that warned of recessionary risks further pressed on market sentiment.2. This sort of activity tends to increase supply pressure, which regularly leads to short-term price weakness for BTC. Why is Ethereum performing worse than Bitcoin? Broader derivatives data showed over $1.05 billion liquidated in the 24 hours leading up to November 6, 2026.
Bitcoin positions accounted for around $267 million in liquidations during the key session.
The most immediate takeaway is about leverage, not direction.
A nearly 6% move in Bitcoin is unremarkable by crypto standards.
The lopsided 88.2% share of long liquidations suggests the market was crowded on one side heading into the drop.

Ethereum had it worse, sliding more than 7% to about $2,247.
Bitcoin hit an intraday low of $74,780.91 on November 6.
That marked its weakest intraday level since August 21.

extraction.body: Crypto traders who bet on higher prices just had a very expensive couple of days. More than $1 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated as Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, and Solana all fell below key price levels. A widely shared market post put the wipeout at $1 billion in just 10 minutes. Broader derivatives data showed over $1.05 billion liquidated in the 24 hours leading up to November 6, 2026. The trigger wasn't a hack, a collapsed exchange, or a rogue tweet. It came from Wall Street, where a sharp selloff in US tech and AI stocks dragged crypto down with it. Bitcoin hit an intraday low of $74,780.91 on November 6. That marked its weakest intraday level since August 21. The world's largest crypto fell nearly 6% during the episode. Ethereum had it worse, sliding more than 7% to about $2,247. XRP and Solana also broke below critical support levels. Long positions accounted for approximately $930 million of the total, or 88.2%. Bitcoin positions accounted for around $267 million in liquidations during the key session. Ethereum followed with approximately $167 million, and XRP and Solana added further losses on top. Nearly 211,000 traders were hit by the liquidations. Most of the damage landed on major exchanges like Binance. The problem is that liquidating a long position means selling. That selling pushes prices lower, which triggers the next batch of liquidations, which means more selling. That chain reaction is how a market can shed $1 billion in leveraged bets in a matter of minutes, as the viral post described. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.5% amid turmoil across AI and chip stocks. Escalating worries about the AI sector's growth prospects collided with uncertainty in the post-midterm election landscape. Bitcoin ETFs added to the pressure. The selloff coincided with hefty outflows from the funds, giving prices another downward shove. Sentiment followed price. The Fear & Greed Index, a popular gauge of crypto market mood, slipped into "fear" territory, resetting the bullish tone that had been building. The most immediate takeaway is about leverage, not direction. A nearly 6% move in Bitcoin is unremarkable by crypto standards. The lopsided 88.2% share of long liquidations suggests the market was crowded on one side heading into the drop. The bigger story for investors is correlation. Crypto's fate this week was decided largely by what happened to AI and chip stocks, not by anything happening on a blockchain. Select market data provided by ICE Data Services . passages: Bitcoin ( CRYPTO: BTC ), XRP ( CRYPTO: XRP ), Ethereum ( CRYPTO: ETH ), and Solana ( CRYPTO: SOL ) are all down 6-8% in a week, and the crypto market has shed over $80 billion in value since March 24.
The Fear & Greed Index sits at 23, and the average crypto RSI has dropped to 39—oversold territory that the market hasn’t seen since early February’s crash.
His work focuses on price levels, spot ETF flows, on-chain data and the regulatory decisions that move crypto markets, written so a first-time buyer and a seasoned trader can both use it.
Sam has written about crypto professionally since 2019 and has published more than 2,000 articles.
Before joining 24/7 Wall St., he wrote for crypto media outlets and Web3 companies and ghostwrote for crypto founders and token launches.
His analysis is syndicated on Yahoo Finance, MSN and AOL and has been cited by other crypto news sites.
When he isn't reading charts, Sam is usually at the gym or watching One Piece, a series he maintains has better tokenomics than most altcoins.
What would point to a recovery or further downturn is Bitcoin’s price action.
If Bitcoin manages to get back to $70,000, it shows the market has shaken off the crash.
But if Bitcoin closes below $66,000 on a daily basis, a move toward $50,000 could be on the cards.
For anyone holding through this, the $66,000 Bitcoin level is what would determine if the crash is stabilising or just getting started.
Every crash driver right now is coming from outside crypto—war, oil, rates, options mechanics.
The assets themselves haven’t broken as ETF flows across Bitcoin, XRP, and Solana pulled in billions in cumulative inflows even through the worst of the selling.
Crypto prices were supposed to be ripping higher today.
Yesterday’s CLARITY Act vote cleared the Senate Banking Committee 15-9—a bipartisan win that sent Bitcoin to $82,000, XRP to $1.55, Solana to $93, and Ethereum…
XRP had its worst quarter in eight years, Ethereum plunged over…
Ethereum broke below $2,000 for the first time since mid-2024, putting it 60% below its August 2025 high of $4,953.
XRP fell to $1.33—down 65% from its July 2025 cycle high of $3.65—even though the SEC recently classified it as a digital commodity .
When Bitcoin falls, XRP tends to take an even bigger hit.
Iran threatened to block the Bab el-Mandeb Strait —the Red Sea gateway that carries 12% of global seaborne oil—on top of the Strait of Hormuz, which has been effectively closed since late February.
Oil pushed above $103, and the gold-to-crypto rotation that had been helping Bitcoin recover earlier in March reversed completely.
Bitcoin ETF outflows hit $171 million on March 26 , and Ethereum ETFs posted $92.5 million in outflows the same day—their seventh consecutive negative session.
Bitcoin dropped from $71,000 at the start of the week to $66,457, marking its lowest level since early March.
On March 27, Deribit settled $14.16 billion in Bitcoin options —the largest quarterly expiry of 2026, wiping out nearly 40% of all open positions on the exchange.
The max pain level sat at $75,000, roughly $9,000 above where Bitcoin was actually trading, meaning most of the bullish positions didn’t pay out.
Bitcoin dropped 5% in 24 hours to as low as $65,720 as the forced selling cascaded through the market.
Over 122,000 traders were liquidated, with total losses reaching $451 million.
The drop has taken the BTC through $100,000, $80,000, and $70,000, but every time the Bitcoin price has…
The fastest way this turns around is a ceasefire or de-escalation in the Iran-Israel war.
The last time ceasefire reports surfaced in early March, Bitcoin recovered 16% in five days—from $63,106 to $73,156.
Oil dropping back below $90 would also relieve the inflation pressure that’s keeping the Fed from cutting rates, and risk appetite would come back across stocks and crypto almost immediately.
As long as oil stays above $100 and the war keeps escalating, it’s hard to see a sustained rally in any risk asset.
By Saturday March 22 it dropped below $68,000 after Trump threatened to obliterate…
Stablecoin supply is sitting near a record $316 billion right now, which tells you that capital hasn’t actually left the crypto ecosystem.
When conditions improve, that money can flow back into BTC, ETH, XRP , and SOL.
If you start seeing ETF inflows turn positive across multiple consecutive days rather than one-off bounces, that’s likely the beginning of a recovery.

Bitcoin ( CRYPTO: BTC ), XRP ( CRYPTO: XRP ), Ethereum ( CRYPTO: ETH ), and Solana ( CRYPTO: SOL ) are all down 6-8% in a week, and the crypto market has shed over $80 billion in value since March 24. The Fear & Greed Index sits at 23, and the average crypto RSI has dropped to 39—oversold territory that the market hasn’t seen since early February’s crash.

The selloff picked up speed after Iran threatened to block a second global oil chokepoint, pushing oil above $100 and sending investors running from risk assets. This came on the same day as the largest crypto options expiry of 2026—$14 billion worth—which triggered over $450 million in liquidations and wiped out more than 122,000 traders.
With the broader crypto market in bearish territory, here’s what we think needs to happen for a recovery.

On March 27, Deribit settled $14.16 billion in Bitcoin options —the largest quarterly expiry of 2026, wiping out nearly 40% of all open positions on the exchange. The max pain level sat at $75,000, roughly $9,000 above where Bitcoin was actually trading, meaning most of the bullish positions didn’t pay out. Bitcoin dropped 5% in 24 hours to as low as $65,720 as the forced selling cascaded through the market. Over 122,000 traders were liquidated, with total losses reaching $451 million.

The expiry alone would have been rough, but it coincided with the worst stretch of the Iran-Israel war for financial markets. Iran threatened to block the Bab el-Mandeb Strait —the Red Sea gateway that carries 12% of global seaborne oil—on top of the Strait of Hormuz, which has been effectively closed since late February. Oil pushed above $103, and the gold-to-crypto rotation that had been helping Bitcoin recover earlier in March reversed completely. Bitcoin ETF outflows hit $171 million on March 26 , and Ethereum ETFs posted $92.5 million in outflows the same day—their seventh consecutive negative session.

All of this is playing out against a macro backdrop that was already working against crypto. The Fed’s March 18 meeting revised its 2026 PCE inflation forecast from 2.4% to 2.7%—the largest single-year upward revision in recent cycles. And this pushed rate cut expectations further out.

The 10-year Treasury yield is now near 4.5%, and the dollar index climbed 0.57% in a week. When yields rise and the dollar strengthens, money moves out of crypto and into bonds. The 15% global tariff overhang that’s been keeping investors away from risk assets since early 2026 hasn’t gone anywhere either, so when the options expired and Iran escalation hit, there was no cushion underneath the market.
Here’s where each asset stands as of March 28, 2026:

Bitcoin dropped from $71,000 at the start of the week to $66,457, marking its lowest level since early March. It’s now 47% below its October 2025 all-time high of $126,080. The $66,000 level is where buyers have stepped in before, and a daily close below it would be the first time Bitcoin has lost that support since the February crash.

Ethereum broke below $2,000 for the first time since mid-2024, putting it 60% below its August 2025 high of $4,953. XRP fell to $1.33—down 65% from its July 2025 cycle high of $3.65—even though the SEC recently classified it as a digital commodity .

Of all four assets, Solana took the biggest hit. SOL is now down 72% from its high, with network transactions dropping 3.2% and active addresses falling 11% over the past month. This marks one of the few cases where on-chain activity is declining alongside the price rather than holding steady.

The fastest way this turns around is a ceasefire or de-escalation in the Iran-Israel war. The last time ceasefire reports surfaced in early March, Bitcoin recovered 16% in five days—from $63,106 to $73,156. Oil dropping back below $90 would also relieve the inflation pressure that’s keeping the Fed from cutting rates, and risk appetite would come back across stocks and crypto almost immediately. As long as oil stays above $100 and the war keeps escalating, it’s hard to see a sustained rally in any risk asset.

On the regulatory side, the CLARITY Act is moving closer to a Senate vote. Senators Tillis and Alsobrooks reached an agreement on the stablecoin yield language that had been stalling progress, and the Banking Committee is now targeting a markup in late April. If it passes, institutions would finally have the legal framework to allocate to crypto at scale—something 65% of surveyed institutional investors said is their top requirement before increasing exposure.

Stablecoin supply is sitting near a record $316 billion right now, which tells you that capital hasn’t actually left the crypto ecosystem. When conditions improve, that money can flow back into BTC, ETH, XRP , and SOL. If you start seeing ETF inflows turn positive across multiple consecutive days rather than one-off bounces, that’s likely the beginning of a recovery.

Every crash driver right now is coming from outside crypto—war, oil, rates, options mechanics. The assets themselves haven’t broken as ETF flows across Bitcoin, XRP, and Solana pulled in billions in cumulative inflows even through the worst of the selling. This shows the market has more institutional backing than any previous downturn, which is why the drops have been sharp but not catastrophic.

What would point to a recovery or further downturn is Bitcoin’s price action. If Bitcoin manages to get back to $70,000, it shows the market has shaken off the crash. But if Bitcoin closes below $66,000 on a daily basis, a move toward $50,000 could be on the cards. And if BTC drops that far, XRP, Ethereum, and Solana would fall as well. For anyone holding through this, the $66,000 Bitcoin level is what would determine if the crash is stabilising or just getting started.

extraction.body: HIGHLIGHTS The New York Stock Exchange has picked Avalanche as the settlement layer for its tokenized stocks trading platform. The stock exchange is targeting a launch by year-end for the platform, pending regulatory approval. Avalanche's AVAX token is up amid this development. The New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) has picked Avalanche as the settlement network for its tokenized stocks platform. This comes as the stock exchange plans to roll out the platform by year-end, pending approval from the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). NYSE Chooses Avalanche For Tokenized Stocks Platform In an X post, Avalanche said the NYSE will build its tokenized stocks platform’s core clearing and settlement layer on its network. "Avalanche will support the platform’s clearing firm, supporting the development of infrastructure for 24/7 trading, clearing, and settlement," the post read. The layer-1 network further described it as a "landmark step toward the next generation of global financial markets." The network will serve as the exclusive settlement layer over top layer-1 networks like Solana and Ethereum, which are known as go-to platforms for tokenization. Meanwhile, NYSE is targeting a launch this quarter for its tokenized stocks platform, pending SEC approval. This comes despite pushback from several companies, including Amazon, Apple, Tesla, and SpaceX, over the stock exchange tokenizing their shares. Ahead of the proposed launch of its tokenized stocks platform, the NYSE has also partnered with transfer agents. As CoinGape reported last week, the NYSE partnered with Broadridge, which will also help provide onchain governance for holders of these tokenized stocks. AVAX Climbs Following Announcement Avalanche's native token AVAX has climbed after the announcement that NYSE picked the network as its exclusive settlement layer. The token is trading at around $8.7, up over 7, according to TradingView data. This comes amid the downtrend in the broader crypto market, with Bitcoin trading below $75,000. Despite its recent rally, AVAX remains down more than 15% in the last month and more than 28% year-to-date (YTD). passages: For the crypto market, the announcement gave Avalanche's native token AVAX a lift, with the coin up about 8% over the prior 24 hours.

For Wall Street, the significance lies in the architecture: a major exchange is outsourcing the book of record for tokenized share settlement to a public blockchain while keeping issuance open to rival networks, a design that could pressure competing venues to disclose similar choices.
Whether the model reaches live trading depends on approvals that have not yet been granted.

Ava Labs said Monday that its infrastructure will underpin the clearing firm behind the NYSE-affiliated alternative trading system (ATS), which is being built to record and settle transactions around the clock.
The venue, which still needs regulatory sign-off, is designed to support equities issued across multiple blockchain networks rather than confining issuance to Avalanche alone.

"At the NYSE, we're looking at how blockchain technology can expand what we offer in equities, and we're picking the right technology for each job," Dennis Lee, the exchange's head of digital issuance, said in a statement.
NYSE first outlined the project in January, proposing to bolt blockchain-based post-trade processing onto its existing Pillar matching engine.
The system is intended to handle tokenized U.S. equities and exchange-traded funds, including securities that exist digitally alongside conventional shares as well as those issued natively as tokens.
Nasdaq is building tokenized stock capabilities, including a partnership with the parent of crypto exchange Kraken to distribute blockchain-based shares internationally.

The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation, which anchors U.S. securities custody and settlement, launched a tokenization service last month built on its private Besu blockchain and the Canton Network, focused on custody and transfers rather than running a trading venue.

A separate route is opening through the Securities and Exchange Commission's innovation exemption, which gives selected blockchain-based venues a path to trade tokenized stocks via automated market makers, with issuers able to opt out.
Separately, ICE has been working with BNY and Citi on tokenized deposits that could let clearing members move funds and meet margin calls outside normal banking hours.

extraction.body: The New York Stock Exchange has chosen the Avalanche network to serve as the core settlement ledger for its planned tokenized securities venue, handing a public blockchain a central role in the exchange operator's effort to move equity trading onchain. Ava Labs said Monday that its infrastructure will underpin the clearing firm behind the NYSE-affiliated alternative trading system (ATS), which is being built to record and settle transactions around the clock. The venue, which still needs regulatory sign-off, is designed to support equities issued across multiple blockchain networks rather than confining issuance to Avalanche alone. "At the NYSE, we're looking at how blockchain technology can expand what we offer in equities, and we're picking the right technology for each job," Dennis Lee, the exchange's head of digital issuance, said in a statement. Lee said the clearing ledger had to combine dependable transaction throughput, predictable costs and controls over network participation while remaining connected to a developed developer ecosystem. "Avalanche meets all those needs," he said. The selection caps roughly a year of technical and commercial vetting by NYSE and its parent, Intercontinental Exchange (ICE). Ava Labs President Charley Cooper said during the Avalanche Summit in New York that the exchange probed the economics of the proposed system as closely as its engineering, noting that "they weren't just kicking the tires on our technology." ICE Head of Strategic Initiatives Michael Blaugrund said at the same event that Avalanche "checks a lot of those boxes for us." Neither company had confirmed a settlement chain at that time. Ava Labs founder and CEO Emin Gün Sirer said the arrangement gives the platform dedicated infrastructure suited to its operational and compliance obligations, pointing to stable transaction costs, permissioned participation and interoperability with other blockchain-based assets as key attributes. NYSE first outlined the project in January, proposing to bolt blockchain-based post-trade processing onto its existing Pillar matching engine. The system is intended to handle tokenized U.S. equities and exchange-traded funds, including securities that exist digitally alongside conventional shares as well as those issued natively as tokens. Investors would be able to submit orders in dollar amounts, buy fractional shares and fund purchases with stablecoins, with access routed through qualified broker-dealers. Holders of eligible tokenized shares would keep standard shareholder rights such as dividends and governance participation. Separately, ICE has been working with BNY and Citi on tokenized deposits that could let clearing members move funds and meet margin calls outside normal banking hours. The Avalanche decision is the latest in a series of agreements covering different layers of the planned digital market. On November 2, NYSE added four transfer agents -- Broadridge Financial Solutions (BR), Computershare, Equiniti and Superstate -- to previously announced partners Securitize and tZERO, bringing the total to six. Broadridge, Computershare and Equiniti together serve close to 5,000 listed companies, including roughly 99% of S&P 500 constituents, handling shareholder records, ownership transfers and corporate actions. ICE struck a deal with tZERO in August covering platform development, blockchain patent licensing and an investment in the company's financing round. The exchange operator has been assembling trading, transfer-agency and settlement components through these separate arrangements ahead of regulatory review. Note: Partner roles as described in company announcements; the platform remains subject to regulatory approval. The move lands in the middle of a broader contest among U.S. market infrastructure providers. Nasdaq is building tokenized stock capabilities, including a partnership with the parent of crypto exchange Kraken to distribute blockchain-based shares internationally. The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation, which anchors U.S. securities custody and settlement, launched a tokenization service last month built on its private Besu blockchain and the Canton Network, focused on custody and transfers rather than running a trading venue. A separate route is opening through the Securities and Exchange Commission's innovation exemption, which gives selected blockchain-based venues a path to trade tokenized stocks via automated market makers, with issuers able to opt out. One such project pairs OKX with ICE; that venue is distinct from the NYSE-affiliated platform. For the crypto market, the announcement gave Avalanche's native token AVAX a lift, with the coin up about 8% over the prior 24 hours. ICE struck a deal with tZERO in August covering platform development, blockchain patent licensing and an investment in the company's financing round. The exchange operator has been assembling trading, transfer-agency and settlement components through these separate arrangements ahead of regulatory review.

Avalanche will provide the ledger used to record and settle transactions through the platform's clearing firm, while the trading venue itself will accommodate equities issued across different blockchain networks. NYSE Head of Digital Issuance Dennis Lee said the exchange had examined several technical requirements before choosing Avalanche for the settlement infrastructure. In September, it was reported that NYSE had spent approximately 12 months testing Avalanche technology and examining how it could work alongside the exchange's existing trading systems. During the Avalanche Summit in New York, Ava Labs President Charley Cooper explained that NYSE had examined the commercial side of the proposed infrastructure alongside its technical capabilities. "They weren't just kicking the tires on our technology," Cooper said at the time, explaining that the exchange wanted to understand whether Ava Labs could meet its business and economic requirements. ICE Head of Strategic Initiatives Michael Blaugrund expressed similar views during the event, saying Avalanche satisfied several requirements the company had established while evaluating blockchain providers. "As we've evaluated different platforms, Avalanche checks a lot of those boxes for us," Blaugrund said. At the time, neither company had confirmed which blockchain would handle settlement for the planned securities venue. Ava Labs founder and CEO Emin Gün Sirer said the newly announced arrangement would provide dedicated infrastructure capable of meeting the platform's operational and regulatory requirements. He described predictable transaction costs, controlled participation and connectivity with other blockchain-based assets as important features of the system. ICE had previously reached an agreement with tZERO in August covering platform development, blockchain patent licensing and an investment in the company's financing round. The exchange operator has been assembling the trading, transfer-agency and settlement components through these separate arrangements as it prepares the digital venue for regulatory review.

extraction.body: HIGHLIGHTS The New York Stock Exchange has picked Avalanche as the settlement layer for its tokenized stocks trading platform. The stock exchange is targeting a launch by year-end for the platform, pending regulatory approval. Avalanche's AVAX token is up amid this development. The New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) has picked Avalanche as the settlement network for its tokenized stocks platform. This comes as the stock exchange plans to roll out the platform by year-end, pending approval from the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). NYSE Chooses Avalanche For Tokenized Stocks Platform In an X post, Avalanche said the NYSE will build its tokenized stocks platform’s core clearing and settlement layer on its network. "Avalanche will support the platform’s clearing firm, supporting the development of infrastructure for 24/7 trading, clearing, and settlement," the post read. The layer-1 network further described it as a "landmark step toward the next generation of global financial markets." The network will serve as the exclusive settlement layer over top layer-1 networks like Solana and Ethereum, which are known as go-to platforms for tokenization. Meanwhile, NYSE is targeting a launch this quarter for its tokenized stocks platform, pending SEC approval. This comes despite pushback from several companies, including Amazon, Apple, Tesla, and SpaceX, over the stock exchange tokenizing their shares. Ahead of the proposed launch of its tokenized stocks platform, the NYSE has also partnered with transfer agents. As CoinGape reported last week, the NYSE partnered with Broadridge, which will also help provide onchain governance for holders of these tokenized stocks. AVAX Climbs Following Announcement Avalanche's native token AVAX has climbed after the announcement that NYSE picked the network as its exclusive settlement layer. The token is trading at around $8.7, up over 7, according to TradingView data. This comes amid the downtrend in the broader crypto market, with Bitcoin trading below $75,000. Despite its recent rally, AVAX remains down more than 15% in the last month and more than 28% year-to-date (YTD). For more on trading tokenized assets, check out Best Platforms & Crypto Exchanges to Trade Pre-IPO Tokens

The venue, which still needs regulatory sign-off, is designed to support equities issued across multiple blockchain networks rather than confining issuance to Avalanche alone. "At the NYSE, we're looking at how blockchain technology can expand what we offer in equities, and we're picking the right technology for each job," Dennis Lee, the exchange's head of digital issuance, said in a statement. Lee said the clearing ledger had to combine dependable transaction throughput, predictable costs and controls over network participation while remaining connected to a developed developer ecosystem. "Avalanche meets all those needs," he said. The selection caps roughly a year of technical and commercial vetting by NYSE and its parent, Intercontinental Exchange (ICE). Ava Labs President Charley Cooper said during the Avalanche Summit in New York that the exchange probed the economics of the proposed system as closely as its engineering, noting that "they weren't just kicking the tires on our technology." ICE Head of Strategic Initiatives Michael Blaugrund said at the same event that Avalanche "checks a lot of those boxes for us." Neither company had confirmed a settlement chain at that time. Ava Labs founder and CEO Emin Gün Sirer said the arrangement gives the platform dedicated infrastructure suited to its operational and compliance obligations, pointing to stable transaction costs, permissioned participation and interoperability with other blockchain-based assets as key attributes. NYSE first outlined the project in January, proposing to bolt blockchain-based post-trade processing onto its existing Pillar matching engine. The system is intended to handle tokenized U.S. equities and exchange-traded funds, including securities that exist digitally alongside conventional shares as well as those issued natively as tokens. Investors would be able to submit orders in dollar amounts, buy fractional shares and fund purchases with stablecoins, with access routed through qualified broker-dealers. Holders of eligible tokenized shares would keep standard shareholder rights such as dividends and governance participation. Separately, ICE has been working with BNY and Citi on tokenized deposits that could let clearing members move funds and meet margin calls outside normal banking hours. The Avalanche decision is the latest in a series of agreements covering different layers of the planned digital market. On November 2, NYSE added four transfer agents -- Broadridge Financial Solutions (BR), Computershare, Equiniti and Superstate -- to previously announced partners Securitize and tZERO, bringing the total to six. Broadridge, Computershare and Equiniti together serve close to 5,000 listed companies, including roughly 99% of S&P 500 constituents, handling shareholder records, ownership transfers and corporate actions. ICE struck a deal with tZERO in August covering platform development, blockchain patent licensing and an investment in the company's financing round. extraction.body: Avalanche has been selected to provide the core blockchain ledger technology for the clearing firm supporting the New York Stock Exchange's upcoming tokenized securities trading platform. NYSE has selected Avalanche to provide the core ledger technology for the clearing firm supporting its upcoming tokenized securities trading platform. Avalanche will handle the recording and settlement of transactions, while the proposed venue is designed to support equities issued across multiple blockchain networks. The selection follows roughly a year of testing by NYSE, during which the exchange evaluated Avalanche's technical capabilities, operating costs and compatibility with its existing infrastructure. The planned platform will support 24/7 trading and onchain settlement of tokenized securities, subject to regulatory approval. NYSE has been working with several technology and transfer agent partners, including Broadridge, Computershare, Equiniti, Securitize and tZERO, to develop the platform. Ava Labs announced on November 9 that its blockchain infrastructure will support the NYSE-affiliated digital alternative trading system (ATS), which is being developed to allow continuous trading and onchain settlement of tokenized securities. The platform remains subject to regulatory approval and is designed to operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week, allowing participating investors to trade securities outside conventional stock market hours. Avalanche will provide the ledger used to record and settle transactions through the platform's clearing firm, while the trading venue itself will accommodate equities issued across different blockchain networks. NYSE Head of Digital Issuance Dennis Lee said the exchange had examined several technical requirements before choosing Avalanche for the settlement infrastructure. According to Lee, the clearing ledger must offer reliable transaction processing, predictable costs and controls over who can participate in the network, while maintaining access to an established developer ecosystem. Avalanche selection follows a year of NYSE testing The announcement follows roughly a year of technical evaluations and discussions between Ava Labs and NYSE parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE). In September, it was reported that NYSE had spent approximately 12 months testing Avalanche technology and examining how it could work alongside the exchange's existing trading systems. During the Avalanche Summit in New York, Ava Labs President Charley Cooper explained that NYSE had examined the commercial side of the proposed infrastructure alongside its technical capabilities. "They weren't just kicking the tires on our technology," Cooper said at the time, explaining that the exchange wanted to understand whether Ava Labs could meet its business and economic requirements. ICE Head of Strategic Initiatives Michael Blaugrund expressed similar views during the event, saying Avalanche satisfied several requirements the company had established while evaluating blockchain providers. "As we've evaluated different platforms, Avalanche checks a lot of those boxes for us," Blaugrund said. At the time, neither company had confirmed which blockchain would handle settlement for the planned securities venue. Ava Labs founder and CEO Emin Gün Sirer said the newly announced arrangement would provide dedicated infrastructure capable of meeting the platform's operational and regulatory requirements. He described predictable transaction costs, controlled participation and connectivity with other blockchain-based assets as important features of the system. How NYSE's tokenized securities platform will operate NYSE first announced the proposed platform in January, outlining plans to combine its existing Pillar matching engine with blockchain-based infrastructure for post-trade processing. The exchange said the system would support tokenized US equities and exchange-traded funds, including securities represented digitally alongside conventional shares and securities issued directly as tokens. NYSE said holders of eligible tokenized shares would retain conventional shareholder rights, including dividends and participation in corporate governance. The proposed venue would provide access through qualified broker-dealers, with the exchange seeking to preserve established securities market requirements within its blockchain-based trading arrangements. ICE has separately been working with BNY and Citi on tokenized deposits that could help clearing members transfer funds and meet margin requirements outside regular banking hours. NYSE expands its network of tokenization partners Avalanche's selection follows several agreements involving companies responsible for different parts of NYSE's planned digital securities infrastructure. On November 2, the exchange added four transfer agents, naming Broadridge Financial Solutions, Computershare, Equiniti and Superstate as partners. The companies joined Securitize and tZERO, bringing the number of participating transfer-agent firms to six. Their responsibilities include maintaining shareholder records, processing ownership changes and supporting corporate actions associated with securities issued or traded through the proposed system. ICE had previously reached an agreement with tZERO in August covering platform development, blockchain patent licensing and an investment in the company's financing round. The exchange operator has been assembling the trading, transfer-agency and settlement components through these separate arrangements as it prepares the digital venue for regulatory review.

extraction.body: Missile explosions struck Kyiv and led to electricity outages early Saturday as Ukraine prepared for trilateral talks with Russia and the United States next Tuesday in Abu Dhabi, capital of the United Arab Emirates. Ukraine's European allies backing the peace initiative are seeking to be involved in the negotiations. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Interfax news agency the Russian delegation, headed again by Kremlin aide Vladimir Medinsky as chief negotiator, will include Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov for the first time and senior General Staff officer Yuri Zhigarlovsky. Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday met with all members of the delegation at a Security Council meeting. During the televised portion of the meeting, Putin thanked the UAE for its consistent help in finding a solution to the Ukrainian crisis and said he wanted to discuss preparations with the Russian team for the upcoming talks. Meanwhile, Russian guided aerial bombs that struck a former school and shelter in the village of Komyshuvakha near the front line in the Zaporizhzhia region on Monday have claimed at least 53 lives to date, according to Ukrainian authorities. Rescuers continued to dismantle the shattered structures and clear the rubble in search of bodies. Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy has appealed to Western allies for more deliveries after Russians forceshammered energy infrastructure around Kyiv with missiles and drones overnight. He stated the challenges of widespread power outages and water cuts are "very serious" for the capital's residents and industry. Zelenskyy announced in his daily briefing new agreements on energy supplies from Germany, Spain and Slovakia and other nations are in place for equipment needed for repairs and reserves. He also issued warning of fresh attacks being prepared against Ukraine's energy sector, bridges across the Dnipro River and civilian infrastructure. Speaking at the Ukrainian Embassy in the US, the Ukrainian Parliament Commissioner for Human Rights Dmytro Lubinets commended the US efforts in brokering a six-day ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Oleshky region and highlighted a major evacuation operation that enabled residents to be transferred to Ukrainian-held territory. The ombudsman said he hoped to expand such humanitarian efforts with the help of Washington. US President Donald Trump said he had meetings with people on Russia and other issues in his Florida resort. "Mar-a-Lago with a lot of different people having to do with Russia and having to do with other things...We just had a very good meeting and we have a lot of good calls made and we're doing very well, so we're working well with Russia, Ukraine. We're making a lot of progress," he said. In Warsaw, the European Union High Representative Kaja Kallas and Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski both stressed it would be impossible to reach a deal to stop the war in Ukraine without the participation of Europe. Sikorski further contended a ceasefire must come first before any kind of negotiation.

extraction.body: Missile explosions struck Kyiv and led to electricity outages early Saturday as Ukraine prepared for trilateral talks with Russia and the United States next Tuesday in Abu Dhabi, capital of the United Arab Emirates. Ukraine's European allies backing the peace initiative are seeking to be involved in the negotiations. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Interfax news agency the Russian delegation, headed again by Kremlin aide Vladimir Medinsky as chief negotiator, will include Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov for the first time and senior General Staff officer Yuri Zhigarlovsky. Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday met with all members of the delegation at a Security Council meeting. During the televised portion of the meeting, Putin thanked the UAE for its consistent help in finding a solution to the Ukrainian crisis and said he wanted to discuss preparations with the Russian team for the upcoming talks. Meanwhile, Russian guided aerial bombs that struck a former school and shelter in the village of Komyshuvakha near the front line in the Zaporizhzhia region on Monday have claimed at least 53 lives to date, according to Ukrainian authorities. Rescuers continued to dismantle the shattered structures and clear the rubble in search of bodies. Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy has appealed to Western allies for more deliveries after Russians forceshammered energy infrastructure around Kyiv with missiles and drones overnight. He stated the challenges of widespread power outages and water cuts are "very serious" for the capital's residents and industry. Zelenskyy announced in his daily briefing new agreements on energy supplies from Germany, Spain and Slovakia and other nations are in place for equipment needed for repairs and reserves. He also issued warning of fresh attacks being prepared against Ukraine's energy sector, bridges across the Dnipro River and civilian infrastructure. Speaking at the Ukrainian Embassy in the US, the Ukrainian Parliament Commissioner for Human Rights Dmytro Lubinets commended the US efforts in brokering a six-day ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Oleshky region and highlighted a major evacuation operation that enabled residents to be transferred to Ukrainian-held territory. The ombudsman said he hoped to expand such humanitarian efforts with the help of Washington. US President Donald Trump said he had meetings with people on Russia and other issues in his Florida resort. "Mar-a-Lago with a lot of different people having to do with Russia and having to do with other things...We just had a very good meeting and we have a lot of good calls made and we're doing very well, so we're working well with Russia, Ukraine. We're making a lot of progress," he said. In Warsaw, the European Union High Representative Kaja Kallas and Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski both stressed it would be impossible to reach a deal to stop the war in Ukraine without the participation of Europe. Sikorski further contended a ceasefire must come first before any kind of negotiation.

sources.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admits affair as company launches investigation into foreign spy claims
passages: Nvidia chief Jensen Huang has admitted to having an extramarital affair as his company announced it will investigate reports he was the “target of a foreign intelligence effort.” The separate statements come amid growing concern over Huang’s close relationship with an executive from Singapore-based tech company Megaspeed, Alice Huang.
“I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it,” Huang, 63, said, adding that he supports Nvidia’s investigation.

But, the board “has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised.” In a note, Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at merchant bank Yorkville & Ives Co., called the news “a black eye moment for Jensen” that will increase scrutiny of chip sales to China, which Huang has previously lobbied for.

Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year.” It added that any concerns about illegal chip diversion were “debunked last year.” Huang joked in a previous interview that he wooed his wife Lori Huang, whom he met in college when he was 17 and she was 19, by offering to help with her homework and vowing to become a CEO by age 30.

“The issue of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge US technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress.” China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Monday that the allegation that Alice Huang was gathering information for Beijing was “purely groundless speculation and an attempt to smear and malign China.” State-run tabloid The Global Times accused US media outlets of making up stories that could derail a detente between the two nations.
The investigation will also cast a shadow over Nvidia’s share price, Ives added, as investors question whether Huang will remain at the helm of the company he helped found.

“I don’t think it will serve the best interests of Nvidia shareholders and industry partners either if Jensen suddenly quits tomorrow.” The US government cleared 10 Chinese firms to buy Nvidia’s second-most powerful AI chips, Reuters reported earlier this year, though its unclear how many chips have actually been sold following the approval.

I think he probably has an excuse for it.” On Thursday, Republican chairmen of three influential House panels — the committees on Foreign Affairs, the Chinese Communist Party and Intelligence — said in a news release that they sent a letter to Huang requesting his appearance before their committees to answer questions about his relationship with Megaspeed and the company’s security protocols against foreign espionage.
Jensen is committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA as CEO without interruption,” a spokesperson for Nvidia told CNN.

The China connection Huang’s connections to Alice Huang and Megaspeed, which buys chips from Nvidia, have come under intense scrutiny as a potential channel for US semiconductors to reach Chinese buyers, despite export controls on advanced technologies.

Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year.” It added that any concerns about illegal chip diversion were “debunked last year.” Huang joked in a previous interview that he wooed his wife Lori Huang, whom he met in college when he was 17 and she was 19, by offering to help with her homework and vowing to become a CEO by age 30. “The issue of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge US technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress.” China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Monday that the allegation that Alice Huang was gathering information for Beijing was “purely groundless speculation and an attempt to smear and malign China.” State-run tabloid The Global Times accused US media outlets of making up stories that could derail a detente between the two nations. extraction.body: Nvidia chief Jensen Huang has admitted to having an extramarital affair as his company announced it will investigate reports he was the “target of a foreign intelligence effort.” The separate statements come amid growing concern over Huang’s close relationship with an executive from Singapore-based tech company Megaspeed, Alice Huang. Several US outlets have reported that American officials suspect Alice Huang, no relation, has fed intelligence to China and helped smuggle advanced artificial intelligence chips into the country. The controversy could undermine faith in the world’s second-largest company and a poster child for the AI boom, at a time when the US and China are racing to surpass the other in technological supremacy. In a note to Nvidia staff, Huang said that he was “unfaithful” and hurt his wife and children. He did not name the other person in the affair. “I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it,” Huang, 63, said, adding that he supports Nvidia’s investigation. “I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security.” Meanwhile, the company said in a Sunday press release that a committee of independent directors and outside counsel will oversee its investigation. “The Board prioritizes US national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders,” the statement said. But, the board “has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised.” In a note, Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at merchant bank Yorkville & Ives Co., called the news “a black eye moment for Jensen” that will increase scrutiny of chip sales to China, which Huang has previously lobbied for. The investigation will also cast a shadow over Nvidia’s share price, Ives added, as investors question whether Huang will remain at the helm of the company he helped found. Jensen is committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA as CEO without interruption,” a spokesperson for Nvidia told CNN. Jacob Ward, a tech journalist and CNN contributor said corporate boards historically tend to oust chief executives caught having extramarital affairs within days. For Nvidia, which holds an outsized role in AI development, global growth and the US stock market, any existential questions about its future will have even greater economic and geopolitical implications. Another unusual factor is that the company has no clear successor for Huang, he added. And this guy who is famously a very, very central commander of all of this stuff, suddenly being caught in this way and especially being caught perhaps being dishonest about it, it’s an incredibly big deal,” Ward said. The China connection Huang’s connections to Alice Huang and Megaspeed, which buys chips from Nvidia, have come under intense scrutiny as a potential channel for US semiconductors to reach Chinese buyers, despite export controls on advanced technologies. The Financial Times previously reported that US intelligence believed that the two were in a romantic relationship. Nvidia said in a past statement that Jensen Huang’s meetings were “not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year.” It added that any concerns about illegal chip diversion were “debunked last year.” Huang joked in a previous interview that he wooed his wife Lori Huang, whom he met in college when he was 17 and she was 19, by offering to help with her homework and vowing to become a CEO by age 30. In 1993 he co-founded Nvidia, which has seen its market capitalization swell to more than $4 trillion as the rise of AI has turbocharged demand for the computer chips it designs. He has since become the face of the company and a prominent figure in the booming business of AI. Huang joined President Donald Trump with a host of other high-profile CEOs in Beijing earlier this year to meet with Chinese leader Xi Jinping. Many people will say Nvidia without Jensen won’t be the same,” George Chen, partner and chair of digital practice at The Asia Group, wrote in a Monday note. “I don’t think it will serve the best interests of Nvidia shareholders and industry partners either if Jensen suddenly quits tomorrow.” The US government cleared 10 Chinese firms to buy Nvidia’s second-most powerful AI chips, Reuters reported earlier this year, though its unclear how many chips have actually been sold following the approval. On Sunday, Trump told reporters that he has not spoken to Huang since Nvidia announced the investigation, but said that he was a “fine person” and praised his contribution to the country. When asked if he wished he had taken action when briefed on the intelligence about alleged spying last year, Trump said, “No I don’t think so. I think he probably has an excuse for it.” On Thursday, Republican chairmen of three influential House panels — the committees on Foreign Affairs, the Chinese Communist Party and Intelligence — said in a news release that they sent a letter to Huang requesting his appearance before their committees to answer questions about his relationship with Megaspeed and the company’s security protocols against foreign espionage. “Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC’s access to sensitive US technology and information,” the chairmen wrote. “The issue of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge US technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress.” China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Monday that the allegation that Alice Huang was gathering information for Beijing was “purely groundless speculation and an attempt to smear and malign China.” State-run tabloid The Global Times accused US media outlets of making up stories that could derail a detente between the two nations. On Chinese social media, Huang’s admission of infidelity became one of the top trending topics with more than 40 million views on the X-like platform Weibo. However, the allegation that Alice Huang was working as a Chinese spy was largely absent from tightly-controlled online discussions.

extraction.body: Nvidia chief Jensen Huang has admitted to having an extramarital affair as his company announced it will investigate reports he was the “target of a foreign intelligence effort.” The separate statements come amid growing concern over Huang’s close relationship with an executive from Singapore-based tech company Megaspeed, Alice Huang. Several US outlets have reported that American officials suspect Alice Huang, no relation, has fed intelligence to China and helped smuggle advanced artificial intelligence chips into the country. The controversy could undermine faith in the world’s second-largest company and a poster child for the AI boom, at a time when the US and China are racing to surpass the other in technological supremacy. In a note to Nvidia staff, Huang said that he was “unfaithful” and hurt his wife and children. He did not name the other person in the affair. “I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it,” Huang, 63, said, adding that he supports Nvidia’s investigation. “I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security.” Meanwhile, the company said in a Sunday press release that a committee of independent directors and outside counsel will oversee its investigation. “The Board prioritizes US national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders,” the statement said. But, the board “has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised.” In a note, Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at merchant bank Yorkville & Ives Co., called the news “a black eye moment for Jensen” that will increase scrutiny of chip sales to China, which Huang has previously lobbied for. The investigation will also cast a shadow over Nvidia’s share price, Ives added, as investors question whether Huang will remain at the helm of the company he helped found. Jensen is committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA as CEO without interruption,” a spokesperson for Nvidia told CNN. Jacob Ward, a tech journalist and CNN contributor said corporate boards historically tend to oust chief executives caught having extramarital affairs within days. For Nvidia, which holds an outsized role in AI development, global growth and the US stock market, any existential questions about its future will have even greater economic and geopolitical implications. Another unusual factor is that the company has no clear successor for Huang, he added. And this guy who is famously a very, very central commander of all of this stuff, suddenly being caught in this way and especially being caught perhaps being dishonest about it, it’s an incredibly big deal,” Ward said. The China connection Huang’s connections to Alice Huang and Megaspeed, which buys chips from Nvidia, have come under intense scrutiny as a potential channel for US semiconductors to reach Chinese buyers, despite export controls on advanced technologies. The Financial Times previously reported that US intelligence believed that the two were in a romantic relationship. Nvidia said in a past statement that Jensen Huang’s meetings were “not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year.” It added that any concerns about illegal chip diversion were “debunked last year.” Huang joked in a previous interview that he wooed his wife Lori Huang, whom he met in college when he was 17 and she was 19, by offering to help with her homework and vowing to become a CEO by age 30. In 1993 he co-founded Nvidia, which has seen its market capitalization swell to more than $4 trillion as the rise of AI has turbocharged demand for the computer chips it designs. He has since become the face of the company and a prominent figure in the booming business of AI. Huang joined President Donald Trump with a host of other high-profile CEOs in Beijing earlier this year to meet with Chinese leader Xi Jinping. Many people will say Nvidia without Jensen won’t be the same,” George Chen, partner and chair of digital practice at The Asia Group, wrote in a Monday note. “I don’t think it will serve the best interests of Nvidia shareholders and industry partners either if Jensen suddenly quits tomorrow.” The US government cleared 10 Chinese firms to buy Nvidia’s second-most powerful AI chips, Reuters reported earlier this year, though its unclear how many chips have actually been sold following the approval. On Sunday, Trump told reporters that he has not spoken to Huang since Nvidia announced the investigation, but said that he was a “fine person” and praised his contribution to the country. When asked if he wished he had taken action when briefed on the intelligence about alleged spying last year, Trump said, “No I don’t think so. I think he probably has an excuse for it.” On Thursday, Republican chairmen of three influential House panels — the committees on Foreign Affairs, the Chinese Communist Party and Intelligence — said in a news release that they sent a letter to Huang requesting his appearance before their committees to answer questions about his relationship with Megaspeed and the company’s security protocols against foreign espionage. “Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC’s access to sensitive US technology and information,” the chairmen wrote. “The issue of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge US technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress.” China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Monday that the allegation that Alice Huang was gathering information for Beijing was “purely groundless speculation and an attempt to smear and malign China.” State-run tabloid The Global Times accused US media outlets of making up stories that could derail a detente between the two nations. On Chinese social media, Huang’s admission of infidelity became one of the top trending topics with more than 40 million views on the X-like platform Weibo. However, the allegation that Alice Huang was working as a Chinese spy was largely absent from tightly-controlled online discussions.
